instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Navigation container joining partial actor-attribute teaching and vector/social-engineering instruction; not a precise single-objective assessment.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: Displayed title matches authored title, but the displayed profile summary replaces the richer authored summary. Core is an instructional label; review-note metadata and objective union are not approval, complete coverage or calibrated difficulty.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Qualified tendencies distinguish actor motive/resources from attribution, and entrusted insider access from malicious, negligent or compromised conduct; defensive context follows.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: Tendencies are qualified, but that warning is behind supporting-detail disclosure. HOLD full actor repair: state sponsorship and strategic purpose are not defined; resources/capability lack comparison criteria; Shadow IT is an alias only; no APT expertise/resource/adaptation explanation, full motive comparison or evidence exercise. Legitimate access/knowledge is a broad insider lens, not proof every knowledgeable outsider is an insider. Compromised credentials alone do not prove deliberate employee harm; a supplier path does not prove the supplier is the malicious actor.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Distinguish reachable exposure from a method/path, then explain supplier lifecycle risks and why signed delivery is not proof of harmless software.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: Exposure and paths can overlap in shorthand; an exposed service is not automatically a distinct vector or confirmed exploit. Signed software needs sound verification and trusted key binding and can still be harmful after build compromise. Supplier governance and defenses are contextual, not a completed assessment, verified build, complete 2.2 coverage or precise 5.3/2.5 assessment.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Six selectable social-engineering patterns compare channel, deception and indicative clues; no actor identity or unique attribution follows from a pattern.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: Clues are not unique classifiers. Email/text/voice are typical channels, not a claim all phishing is email. BEC need not use malware or a truly compromised mailbox. HOLD precise typosquatting/IDN-homograph equivalence: spelling and Unicode look-alikes should be distinguished rather than assigned one universal name. Deceptive intent distinguishes disinformation; accidental sharing does not by itself prove misinformation. No glossary definition is dispositioned.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Five broad delivery categories connect illustrative clues with first defensive thoughts; network attack indicators and mitigation context go beyond pure 2.2 vocabulary.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: Network rows name on-path/DNS/ARP/DDoS indicators from 2.4; physical/social cues and defensive controls mix scopes. HOLD a pure 2.1 or complete 2.2/2.4/2.5 mapping. Authenticate/segment/monitor shorthand is not a universal DDoS or ARP fix; no control was implemented or tested.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Three definitions distinguish a harm-capable person/group, reachable exposure and deceptive messaging; mixed actor/vector vocabulary, not detailed actor decisions.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: Broad accidental-harm wording needs intent context; it does not make every accidental person a malicious actor. Surface and phishing are 2.2 support; the shared profile chip does not turn them into 2.1 actor mastery or teach missing resources, sponsorship or Shadow IT.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Three reminders separate BEC persuasion from mandatory malware, look-alike registration from poisoned resolution, and likely motive from reliable attribution.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: Mixed narrow2.2 naming/deception reminders and2.1 attribution warning; not an exclusive motive-to-identity rule, actual payment incident, DNS experiment or fresh actor family.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: A reveal-only naming example contrasts confusingly similar domain registration with poisoned DNS answers; no submitted actor response or grading.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: The supplied look-alike-registration premise supports narrow2.2 instructional naming contrast. Urgency does not identify sponsor, capability or actor family. Clicking reveal is not an evaluated response, transfer check, completed intervention or recovery.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Derived definition recall from the same three-entry mixed keyword guide; whole-guide context only, not a keyed canonical assessment or actor-attribute decision.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: Equality against supplied definitions measures local recall only. Alternative feedback repeats guide meanings, not actor-specific scenario correction. Whole-guide links are unkeyed at weight0; local maximum score, repeats, self-mark and reveal do not create trusted evidence, fresh families or observed recovery.
